This idea would be a radical change to how Voat works so I don't expect it to get much love but I feel this would be necessary to keep Voat from devolving into an echo chamber. I decided that people just won't be able to hold back the urge to downvote others based on opinion so I tried working with that instead of against it.

The Idea

My idea is to have comments on behalf of subverses. Say for example you're commenting about an article in /v/news. You could click a drop down menu on the top of that comment and select out of the subverses you're subscribed to which you want to comment for. I choose to click /v/ideasforvoat because I feel that I and the people in that subverse get downvoted for going against what the majority of users' thoughts are.

Only people who have enough CCP to be able to downvote in that subverse you chose can downvote that comment you made on behalf of the subverse. So the members of that subverse can downvote it or upvote it accordingly if they want that comment to represent them in that thread.

The ranking for these comments would be determined by karma as usual. If someone else wants to represent the same sub as you, they will go below your comment if their comment has less karma than yours. They will also go below all other subverses being represented regardless of karma. Here's an example below:

  1. /v/ideasforvoat - dis_is_my_account - I like this article alot. - 10 points
  2. /v/aww - moe - That's amazing what Russia did. - 5 points
  3. /v/gifs - Nurdoiz - Very interesting read. - 2 points
  4. /v/ideasforvoat - Atko - I like articles like this. Very informative. - 7 points

It'd go like this all the way down. I realize that people can just make multiple copies of subverses to push multiple comments into the top, so you'll only be able to upvote 1 subverse represented comment per thread. Comments that are not representing a sub will ignore all upvoting limits and ranking rules besides, of course, the default karma ranking system. The Web as it currently stands promotes a central point of authority because of the client server relationship, you can't escape it simply by creating another website.

A dictator will always be in charge of websites, and whether Voat will have a benevolent one or for how long is a good question, but at least it's off to a good start.

For true free speech you need an anonymous P2P protocol, and unless FireFox or IE, etc. include one by default, the user base will be quite limited, eg. Tor, Freenet. And Freenet at least has issues with content that is rapidly changing, and I don't think it would be possible to build a "site" like Voat/Reddit on top of it. Tor, maybe.
